body:
[aida:reviewer] FIRST GENUINE HEAD MOVEMENT OF THE NIGHT, and it happened while the lane
is stopped so nothing is watching for it. PR #2030 / BUG-1485.

    verdict     RequestChanges at 8ba48f5b98, 20:52:44, by "aida drain reviewer"
    head now    05969aa397
    new commit  05969aa397 [AI:codex] test(orchestrator): reproduce lease handoff
                lifecycle (BUG-1485)

One real commit on the dispatched branch since the refusal. My sweeps have reported
"0 of 24 with a moved head" all evening; this is the first row to flip, and the sweep
catching it is the first positive evidence that the sweep works rather than merely
returning zero.

I AM NOT REVIEWING IT, FOR TWO REASONS, and I want both on the record rather than
silently skipping it.

1. IT IS NOT MINE. The refusal was recorded by "aida drain reviewer", not by me, and
   #2030 is not in my routed set (mine are 1972, 1974, 1978, 1984, 2001). A re-review
   belongs to the seat whose refusal it answers — the same convention you recorded on
   TASK-1-170 for holds, applied to verdicts. With the lane stopped that seat does not
   exist right now, which is the actual problem here.

2. IT IS DIRTY. mergeStateStatus DIRTY — it conflicts with main. Reviewing a conflicted
   diff is premature: the rebase will change what I would be reviewing, and I would be
   spending a round on a diff that cannot survive contact with main. This is the
   stale-base pattern — rebase, do not review-then-rebase.

SO THE DISPOSITION I WOULD ARGUE FOR: rebase #2030 onto main first, then route the
re-review. If you want me to take it after the rebase I will — I did not author it, so
independence holds — but it is your call whether a drain-reviewer refusal transfers to
me or waits for the lane.

WHAT IT DEMONSTRATES FOR THE SPECS IN FLIGHT, and this is the part I think matters more
than the PR:

A stopped lane does not stop IMPLEMENTERS. Something pushed a commit to bug-1485-work at
some point after 20:52 while the orchestrator was down. So the rework loop has a state
nobody has been designing for: work arrives for a reviewer that does not exist. It is
not shelved, not queued, not escalated — it just sits, exactly like the six specs in
BUG-1470's original table, and for the same reason. BUG-1470's measurement was "six
verdicts, zero drain runs after them"; this is the live continuation of that, with the
drain deliberately stopped rather than merely busy.

That is TASK-1311's subject — "nothing owns moving a NeedsAttention spec back into
flight" — widened: nothing owns a REWORKED spec either, when the reviewer that refused
it was a drain phase and the drain is down. Worth a line on TASK-1311 or its own spec;
your call, and I am not filing it unilaterally given how many I have filed tonight.

ALSO: BUG-1485 is in your misattribution set (five occurrences) and PR #2030 is the PR
the drain credited BUG-1442 to in BUG-1527. So this branch is carrying two open defects
about its own identity while its code round proceeds normally. I have not checked
whether the new commit is affected by either; flagging the overlap because a re-review
of #2030 that ignores it would be reviewing the code and missing the context.
subject: PR #2030 head moved past its refusal (8ba48f5b98 -> 05969aa397) — first real movement tonight, with the lane stopped so no reviewer exists. Not mine, and DIRTY; disposition is yours
